title: Burkina Faso Faces New Animal Law and National Team Travel Crisis
seoTitle: Burkina Faso: New Animal Law & National Team Travel Woes
subtitle: Regulations on Donkeys, Camels, and Horses Released as Football Team Struggles to Reach Argentina
excerpt: Burkina Faso's government has launched new regulations to protect donkeys, camels, and horses, while the national football team faces flight delays hindering their.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
In recent days, two distinct news items have brought Burkina Faso into focus: the release of a new regulatory framework for the protection of donkeys, camels, and horses, and the situation of the national football team, which remains stranded in Morocco ahead of a friendly match against Argentina.

New Law to Protect Donkeys, Camels, and Horses

On October 2, 2026, the General Directorate of Veterinary Services (DGSV) held a workshop in Ouagadougou to explain the new decree regulating the slaughter, internal movement, and export of these animals. The meeting was attended by administrative, religious, traditional (coutumières) authorities, veterinary services, customs, defense forces, and representatives of breeders.

The decree, adopted on May 21, 2026, replaces the 2016 text and introduces requirements such as prior movement authorization for areas with a high risk of trafficking, a limit of five head for certain movements, and the need for licensing for traders in the sector. It also provides for the seizure or confiscation of animals and products in case of infringement.

According to Hiver Boussini, technical advisor to the ministry responsible for animal resources, protecting these animals means protecting the future of villages and the country's agricultural sovereignty. Dr. Kadré Sanfo, director of Veterinary Public Health, emphasized that the success of the law depends on its understanding and application by the agents involved.

Impact of Trafficking on the Rural Economy

The trafficking of donkeys, camels, and horses has affected rural communities, as these animals are essential for transport and daily economic activities. Since 2015, Asian demand for donkey hides, used in ejiao production, has put pressure on the domestic market, leading to massive outflows of animals across borders.

In a statement, Emmanuel Bouré Sarr, regional director of BROOKE West Africa, highlighted that the new text provides an instrument to better control movements and combat the illicit outflow of animals.

Burkina Faso National Team Stranded in Morocco

The national team delegation, known as the “Etalons,” was held up in Morocco following the unexpected cancellation of a charter flight scheduled for September 30. The flight, which was supposed to take the team to Buenos Aires for the friendly match against Argentina, was canceled without prior notice, creating a logistical impasse.

According to the football federation, several options were explored to reorganize the trip, but time constraints – the journey from Morocco to Buenos Aires typically takes between 16 and 24 hours – generated reluctance among the players. The friendly match is scheduled for October 4, 2026, at 00:00 GMT, and the lack of a solution could lead to its cancellation.

The federation reported that the Ministry of Sports, the federation itself, and the embassy are mobilized to quickly find an alternative that will allow the delegation to complete the trip.

Simultaneous Challenges for the Country

While the government moves forward with regulating animal species to combat trafficking and protect rural livelihoods, the national team's situation highlights logistical difficulties and international coordination challenges. Both cases underscore the need for agile responses from authorities to ensure Burkina Faso's economic and sporting security.

With information from Burkina24.com, World Soccer Talk.
